message.content:
**Uno – Quick Overview** | What | How it works | |------|--------------| | **Goal** | Be the first player to score 500 points (or whatever you set). Points come from the cards left in opponents’ hands when someone goes “Uno.” | | **Deck** | 108 cards: 4 colors (red, yellow, green, blue) × 25 cards each (numbers 0‑9 + two of each action card). 8 Wild cards and 8 Wild Draw Four cards. | | **Setup** | Shuffle, deal 7 cards to each player. Place the remaining cards face‑down as the draw pile; flip the top card to start the discard pile. | | **Turn** | 1️⃣ Play a card that matches either color or number (or an action card).
2️⃣ If you can’t play, draw one card. If that card is playable, you may play it immediately. | | **Action Cards** | • **Skip** – next player loses a turn.
• **Reverse** – changes direction of play.
• **Draw Two** – next player draws two cards and skips a turn.
• **Wild** – you choose the new color.
• **Wild Draw Four** – you choose the new color; next player draws four cards and skips a turn (must be played only if you have no matching color). | | **Winning a Round** | When a player discards their last card, they shout “Uno!” if they’re down to one card. If they forget, the next player must draw two penalty cards. | | **Scoring** | Add up the point values of all cards left in opponents’ hands: numbers = face value, Skip/Reverse/Draw Two = 20, Wild/Wild Draw Four = 50. | | **Next Round** | Shuffle the discard pile into a new draw pile. The winner of the previous round starts the next round. | **Key Tips** * Keep track of what cards have been played to anticipate opponents’ moves. * Use Wild Draw Four strategically—save it for when you really need to block a strong opponent. * Remember the “Uno” rule: if you’re down to one card and forget to say “Uno,” you’ll pay a penalty. That’s the core of Uno! Feel free to tweak the scoring or add house rules for extra fun.
